source.integrity_rule: sha256 of the downloaded archive must match the matching line of the official checksums asset before the provider may run

invocation.environment_rule: unset inherited provider config overrides so the pinned provider default rule set is the one actually assessed

git_history_scan: Commits reachable from the target repository HEAD, assessed from per-commit added lines (provider git log -p mode).
Other refs, stashes, and content that never appears as an added line (for example some merge resolutions) are not covered.
Uncommitted working-tree content is not covered by this scope.
worktree_scan: Regular files present in the target working tree at scan time, assessed as a plain directory (provider --no-git mode).
The provider's directory mode skips the .git directory, so committed history and other refs are not covered by this scope.

known_exclusions: On a target that is not a Git repository this provider does not fail: history mode scans no commits and exits clean, so Shield rejects the target instead of recording that empty result as PASS.
Provider default configuration allowlists (for example binary and lockfile paths) apply unchanged.
Provider rule coverage only; no custom rule set is supplied in this slice.
limitations: Detection is bounded by the pinned provider rule set and its entropy and allowlist behaviour; absence of findings is not proof that no credential exists.
Secret values are redacted and are not retained in Shield evidence; only rule, file, line, and commit references are kept.
Runtime secret stores, credential validity, and protected-data access paths are not assessed.
failure_cases: version output does not match the pinned provider version
provider exits non-zero without establishing findings, including partial scans
provider report is missing or cannot be parsed
